L419@P6: In contrast, our algorithm requires less than 186 or 69 MB (depending on the parameter
L420@P6: set) of additional sanitization key. Furthermore, [BI22] needs to sample a “fresh” RLWE
L421@P6: ciphertext for every external product in the blind rotation step. As reported in [BI22]
L422@P6: sampling a single RLWE ciphertext takes approximately 45 seconds, and they need to
L423@P6: sample 612 to perform a single bootstrapping operation. That gives us 7.6 hours to
L424@P6: perform the sampling. To overcome the timing issue, the authors assume that the RLWE
L425@P6: ciphertexts and Gaussian are precomputed, and the machine has unrestricted memory
L426@P6: and precomputation. However, to make the computation feasible on a laptop they test
L427@P6: the algorithm by reusing a single RLWE ciphertext. Even with the precomputed values,
L428@P6: deterministic bootstrapping takes 3.15 seconds, and sanitization bootstrapping takes
L429@P6: between 21 and 4.68 seconds depending on how many Gaussian samples were precomputed.
L430@P6: In comparison, our deterministic bootstrapping takes 0.14 or 0.27 seconds, sanitization
L431@P6: takes between 0.9 and 1.3 seconds. Most importantly, we do not need any precomputation
L432@P6: for our algorithms to be efficient, and all random variables are generated on-the-fly.
